200
Regional reservation in Karnataka
*661. DR. (Ms.) P. SELVIE DAS: Will
the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
of Karnataka has forwarded a proposal for
amendment of Constitution for providing
regional reservation in Karnataka in the field
of education, employment etc.;
(b) if so, the details of the action taken
in this regard;
(c) whether any similar requests have
been received by Government from other
States; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Cumulative losses of CPSUs
*662. SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA:
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES
AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
cumulative losses of 43 Central PSUs for
the last ten years stand at Rs. 34,261 crores
as on 31st March, 2001;
(b) whether 76.12 per cent of these
losses are by five major PSUs, which are
continuing to operate in spite of incurring
heavy losses; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken by Government to improve their
working?
Approval of TV serials
*663. SHRI HARENDRA SINGH
MALIK: Will the Minister
of INFORMATION AND BROAD-
CASTING be pleased to state:
(a) the details of norms adopted for
giving approval to TV serials;
(b) whether many irregularities have
been noticed in this regard; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken by Government against guilty
persons/officers?
Staff for Fast Track Courts
*664. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of  LAW, JUSTICE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Fast Track
Courts do not have adequate staff; and

(b) if so, how can they be expected to
function efficiently and really work as Fast

FDI in real estate
*665. SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the housing industry which
will have to construct around 6.5 million
dwelling units per year till 2010 to meet the
Prime Minister's 'Shelter for all' has made a
strong plea to Government to allow Foreign
Direct Investment in the real estate sector;
(b) if so, whether they have also called
for a reduction in the steep stamp duty
imposed by the States;
(c) if so, whether any programme in
this regard has been worked out by
Government; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Anti-piracy body for film and music
industries
*666. SHRI C. P. THIRUNAVUK-
KARASU: Will the Minister
of INFORMATION AND BROAD-
CASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to set-
up a National Anti-piracy Umbrella Body
for the film and music industries, as
suggested by the CII-Errot and Young
Report on Entertainment;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the details of other recommendations
made in the report and the reaction of
Government thereto?
Compensation to gardener killed in
terrorists attack
†*667. DR. A.K. PATEL: Will the
Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT
AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the officers
of C.P.W.D. are refusing even to talk to the
family members of the gardener of their
Department who was killed by the
terrorists in Parliament House on
13th December, 2001;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
family has not received any assistance from
the aforesaid Department, so far; and
(c) if so, the reasons therefor and
whether Government propose to issue
urgent orders for providing financial
assistance to the said family?
Reports of National Minorities
Commission
†*668. DR. ABRAR AHMED: Will the
Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of reports of National
Minorities Commission which have not
been presented in Parliament and by when
the same would be presented;
(b) whether Government have taken any
action on the said reports; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
National Illness Assistance Fund
*669. SHRI K.M. KHAN: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the total grant-in-aid released to
States under National Illness Assistance
Fund during the last three years;

Construction of roads in NE States
4798. SHRI RISHANG KEISHING:
Will the Minister of DEVELOPMENT OF
NORTH EASTERN REGION be pleased
to state:
(a) the list of roads under construction
by the North Eastern Council in the North
East, State-wise;
(b) the number of on-going construction
of roads with schedule date/time for
completion; and
(c) the number of new roads approved
and to be taken up soon?
Development of Dhodar
Ali Road
4799. SHRI DRUPAD BORGOHAIN:
Will the Minister of DEVELOPMENT OF
NORTH EASTERN REGION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether North-Eastern Council has
allotted fund for the development of Dhodar
Ali Road from Deberapar of Jorhat district
to Jeypore of Dibrugarh district for the year
2002-2003;
(b) if so, the amount allocated therefor;
(c) whether there is any time -frame
to complete the construction of all
bridges now half done and road
improvement that remains of the other
half of Dhodar Ali Road from
Kamargaon of Golaghat district to
Deberapar of Jorhat district; and
(d) the cause of this delay though the
money was sanctioned in 1989?
NEC Amendment Bill
4800. DR. ARUN KUMAR SARMA:
Will the Minister of DEVELOPMENT OF
NORTH EASTERN REGION be pleased
to state:
(a) the reasons for inordinate delay in
bringing the NEC Amendment Bill after
getting views of NECM's Forum, NEMP's
Forum as well as recommendation of the
Standing Committee on Home Affairs;
(b) whether it is likely to be introduced
during the on-going B udget Session; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?

Amount transferred to non-lapsable
pool
4801. DR. ARUN KUMAR SARMA:
Will the Minister of DEVELOPMENT OF
NORTH EASTERN REGION be pleased
to state:
(a) the list of Ministries which have not
complied with national commitment through
various MP's Special Packages for NER
indicating actual percentage of budgetary
provisions made, utilized and amount
transferred to non-lapsable pool of resources
during last three financial years; and
(b) the action taken on Ministries
Departments not complying with this
national commitment?
Disinvestment of NLC
4802. SHRI C. RAMA-
CHANDRAIAH:
PROF. M. SANKARA-
LINGAM:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Disinvestment
Commission has recommended disinvest-
ment in Neyveli Lignite Corporation
(NLC);
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether NLC is a profit-making PSU
in Tamil Nadu;
(d) if so, the reasons for disinvestment
of profit making PSU; and
(e) the policy enunciated by Government
in regard to disinvestment in profit-making
PSUs?
Disinvestment Policy
†4803. SHRI JANESHWAR
MISHRA: Will the Minister of
DISINVESTMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
ignore the basic facts while carrying out
disinvestment/privatisation;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) the main issues Government consider
while adopting policies for privatisation; and
(d) whether it is also a fact that instead
of competing with full potential in world
market we are selling our factories and
income generating sources to the rich nations
of the world?
Non-payment of dues to suppliers of
raw materials
4804. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether while disinvesting Public
Sector Enterprises, Government ensure that
suppliers of raw materials of small scale
industries are paid in full; and
(b) if so, the reasons why raw material
suppliers to Hindustan Cables Ltd. have not
been paid?
Disinvestment of SCI
4805. SHRI LAJPAT RAI: Will the
Minister of DISINVESTMENT be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
disinvest their stake in Shipping
Corporation of India (SCI);
(b) if so, the percentage of stake to be
disinvested;
(c) whether the employees of the
Corporation are against the disinvestment;
(d) whether the value of shares has been
evaluated; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Disinvestment Commission
4806. SHRI RUMANDLA RAMA-
CHANDRAIAH: Will the Minister of
DISINVESTMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has constituted
the Disinvestment Commission;
(b) if so, the main purposes of this
Commission;
(c) to what extent this Commission
considers the interest of workers; employees
and other stakeholders in public sector units;
and
(d) to what extent its recommendations
are given due consideration for
disinvestment?
